title: From 1895 to 1929
subtitle: Part 01
description: The visionaries, inventors and dreamers. The experiments and discoveries of Georges Méliès, the unique humor of Chaplin and Keaton, surrealism in Germany, the fight for a voice with the Race Films, and the romance and spectacle of 1920s Hollywood.

image.content_description: Scene from A Trip to the Moon, in which a moon with a human face is hit in the right eye by a rocket.

presentation_image.content_description: Scene from The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari, in which a man suspiciously examines a woman's body on the floor.

title: From 1930 to 1939
subtitle: Part 02
description: With the arrival of the talkies, new ways of telling stories were discovered. Hollywood horror entered one of its golden ages with so-called “Gothic horror”. After developing many shorts, Disney released the first animated feature film. The war drastically affected cinema, the romantic comedy took its first shape and gangster films grew even more prominent on the big screen.

image.content_description: Promotional photo from Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, with the title character holding an apple.

presentation_image.content_description: Still from The Wizard of Oz, with the four main characters walking arm in arm.

quote.quote: I've a feeling we're not in Kansas anymore.
quote.author: The Wizard of Oz

quote: Charlie Chaplin and I had a friendly rivalry: who could make a film with the fewest title cards?
author: Buster Keaton

title: From 1940 to 1959
subtitle: Part 03
description: Asian cinema gained even more prominence with the release of several masterpieces. Film noir emerged and musicals kept shining on the big screen. The Western held its reign as one of the most popular genres, and one of cinema's most important movements took place in France: the French New Wave.

image.content_description: Scene from Seven Samurai, with all the characters looking in one direction, ready for battle.

presentation_image.content_description: Scene from Singin' in the Rain, with the main character singing in the rain.

quote.quote: There's nothing between us. There's never been anything between us. Just air.
quote.author: Singin' in the Rain

title: From 1960 to 1969
subtitle: Part 04
description: Brazil caught the world's attention with its Cinema Novo, the sexual revolution of the '60s was reflected on screen, psychological horror gained ground, and science fiction, with 2001: A Space Odyssey, won over audiences and critics.

image.content_description: Photo of HAL 9000 from 2001: A Space Odyssey.

presentation_image.content_description: Profile photo of the couple from Bonnie and Clyde.

quote.quote: Its origin and purpose, still a total mystery.
quote.author: Mission Control's final line

title: From 1970 to 1989
subtitle: Part 05
description: The Exorcist was released, taking horror films to another level. Jaws hit theaters and, at the same time, auteur cinema flourished with Martin Scorsese and other great directors. Then, in the '80s, we saw excellent low-budget productions and era-defining comedies.

image.content_description: Photo of Regan possessed by the demon in The Exorcist.

presentation_image.content_description: Photo of Travis Bickle in Taxi Driver.

quote: Today, more than ever, we need to listen to one another and understand how we see the world, and cinema is the best way to do that.
author: Martin Scorsese

title: From 1990 to 2009
subtitle: Part 06
description: '90s independent cinema dominated the screens, and animation broke new ground with Pixar. CGI reached a new level with The Matrix, and Latin American and European cinema caught the world's attention.

image.content_description: Photo of Vincent and Jules back to back in Pulp Fiction.

presentation_image.content_description: Photo of WALL·E looking at the stars.

quote.quote: I don't want to survive. I want to live!
quote.author: WALL·E

title: From 2010 to 2019
subtitle: Part 07
description: 3D takes over the big screen and superheroes take over the global box office. Horror gets a makeover with The Conjuring and The Witch, animation goes far beyond Disney, films in other languages win over the Oscars right up to Parasite's historic night, and streaming quietly creeps in, winning over audiences, critics and major directors.

presentation_image.content_description: Photo of Baby in Baby Driver.

quote.quote: There's nothing wrong with being a little quiet.
quote.author: Baby Driver

title: From 2020 to today
subtitle: Part 08
description: The pandemic turns the screens dark and streaming goes to war, all the way to the megamergers. Hollywood stops on strike and debates artificial intelligence, social media and internet creators decide the hits, horror becomes the safest bet and cinema from all over the world, from Brazil to Korea, reaches the top of the Oscars.

image.content_description: Fernanda Torres, Selton Mello and their children on the beach, in I'm Still Here.

presentation_image.content_description: Michael B. Jordan in front of a red sun, in Sinners.

quote.quote: Once you overcome the one-inch-tall barrier of subtitles, you will be introduced to so many more amazing films.
quote.author: Bong Joon Ho (Golden Globes, 2020)
